name: Four climax/break structures for 8-bar phrased tracks: (1) committed turnaround, where the last part of an 8-bar loop is cut and deconstructed before the next section restarts; (2) linear rise, an 8-bar section with most elements removed that only builds (filters open, decay/release and reverb/delay times lengthen, new layers enter) until the full section returns; (3) trilogy break: fall (strip chords/rhythm to a few disorienting elements, optionally introduce a new chord progression), rise (percussion and opening filters build), hang (withhold the expected return for a bar with one unique phrase, then return); (4) double trilogy, where a long fall/rise is followed by a short fall/rise inside the same break
goal: Give ambient/cinematic and electronic tracks deliberate build/breakdown shapes. Delta vs arrangement-loop-to-song cluster (8-bar build template, breakdown after a drop, rule of three, no-riser transitions): a named vocabulary of four break shapes with an energy curve for each, the 'hang' withholding trick, and the rule to insert hang time last so the grid stays intact while arranging.

source.title: How to climax in electronic music

prerequisites: A DAW arrangement with an 8-bar-phrased loop or a finished main section
Filter, reverb and delay automation lanes

inputs.name: main_section
inputs.description: The full section the break leads back into

inputs.name: hang_element
inputs.description: One unique phrase (pad swell, single chord, vocal or melodic line) for the hang

outputs.name: break_section
outputs.description: A turnaround, linear rise, trilogy or double-trilogy break with drawn automation

outputs.name: energy_map
outputs.description: Bar-by-bar energy curve (down/up) for the break

constraints: Ambient adaptation: build tension with filter opening, longer reverb/delay and added sustained layers, not snare rolls, rapid stutters or clicky fills (Matt's preference).
Risers stay steady in pitch: use noise/filter sweeps or layered sustained notes, not pitch-glide risers.
If the track has drums, they enter early (~8 counts / ~12 s); only pad/texture before that (Matt's preference).
Insert hang time last (insert-time command), after the rest of the arrangement is done, because it shifts everything after it off the bar grid.
Ableton/MIDI-friendly: every part is a MIDI clip or a resampled audio clip; automation lanes are drawn, not random.
Portable module mapping: section = clip/scene/pattern; rise = filter cutoff + reverb send + layer gain ramps; works in any DAW, a tracker or a Web Audio scheduler.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Phrase the track in 8-bar loops and mark section boundaries.

Committed turnaround: at the end of an 8-bar loop, cut the last bar or two of the loop and deconstruct it (drop elements, filter or reverb-throw what remains), then restart the next section; swap a couple of elements in or out at that point.
steps.expect: A section ending that commits to tension instead of a one-hit variation

steps.action: Linear rise: take an 8-bar section, remove most elements, then from the moment of removal build continuously: open low-pass filters, lengthen decay/release, raise reverb/delay time and send, and bring in new sustained layers or a noise sweep, so energy releases when the full section returns.
steps.expect: One-direction build like drawing a bow

steps.action: Trilogy break, chapter 1 (fall): coming out of a full section, remove chords and most rhythm, leaving a few elements; hold 4-8 bars. Optionally introduce a new chord progression here, kept low in energy.
Chapter 2 (rise): 4-8 bars of building: percussion returns, filters open, sustained layers and noise sweeps enter.
Chapter 3 (hang): where the full section would return, withhold it for about a bar with one unique element (a single pad swell, chord or phrase), then bring the full section back.
steps.expect: Brief suspended moment before the release

steps.action: Double trilogy: inside one break, do a long fall + rise, then where the return is expected do a second, shorter fall + rise before the section comes back (filters can bring percussion back in).
When the arrangement is otherwise finished, insert the hang bar(s) with insert-time so everything after shifts together.
steps.expect: Grid stays intact until the last step

verification: Each break shape has a written down/up energy curve and the automation follows it.
Rises use filter/reverb/layer automation only; no snare rolls or pitch-glide risers.
The hang is inserted last and the following section starts on its own downbeat.
